page.content:
Nineteenth-century aphid plague that destroyed ungrafted European vineyards.

How Phylloxera connects

  • Item: Vitis vinifera — Phylloxera destroyed ungrafted Vitis vinifera vineyards across Europe.
  • Topic: Old World wine — Phylloxera forced Old World growers to graft onto American rootstocks.

What is Phylloxera?

Daktulosphaira vitifoliae ate Vitis vinifera roots across Europe. The fix was grafting vinifera scions onto resistant American rootstocks — a biological occupation of the Old World vineyard.

Key threads lead to Vitis vinifera and Old World wine.
